name: What a Data Privacy Agreement Must Say
title: What a Data Privacy Agreement Must Say
answer: A data privacy agreement is the contract that places an education company under the school's direct control, and for AI tools it must state that student data is used only to provide the service, is not used to train general AI models, is deleted when the contract ends or the school asks, and is limited to listed data fields. It matters because it gives schools, including small districts, enforceable terms over how student information is handled.

crumbs.name: Privacy, Safety, and the Human Review Rule

sections.body: The idea is that a data privacy agreement is the binding contract that puts an education company under the school's direct control. It solves the problem of schools having little leverage over vendors that collect student information. Model agreements are published by many states and consortia, and districts can often sign one already negotiated by another district through the Student Data Privacy Consortium registry. That approach saves time and gives small districts the same protections as large ones. The agreement should be signed by the legal team or a designated administrator, not by an individual teacher.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a school or district, the agreement is handled at the administrative level rather than by a classroom teacher. The legal team or a designated administrator signs it, which keeps the commitment with the institution. Districts can adopt a model agreement or one already negotiated by another district through the Student Data Privacy Consortium registry, which is especially useful for small districts that lack their own negotiating capacity. For AI tools, the terms that matter most are that the company uses student data only to provide the service, does not use it to train general AI models, deletes it when the contract ends or when the school asks, and lists exactly which data fields it collects. The text does not give grade band variations for this idea.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no research evidence for this idea. It refers to the data field listing as the part that raised concerns in Portland, as Figure 3.4 shows, but it states no study, figure or finding beyond that reference. The idea therefore rests on practice and on the model agreements published by states and consortia rather than on research presented in the text.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The limits in the text are about who holds authority and what the contract must secure. Signing stays with the legal team or a designated administrator, not an individual teacher, so a single staff member does not commit the school. The agreement must restrict the company to using student data only to provide the service, must prevent that data from training general AI models, must require deletion when the contract ends or when the school asks, and must list exactly which data fields are collected. The text notes that the data field listing is the part that raised concerns in Portland, as Figure 3.4 shows. Nothing here is legal advice; it describes practice.
